decision: Existing signals support one bounded public observation: after the real auth-add child reaches the fake OAuth token-response barrier, release that successful add response while keeping the expired-chat refresh response held, then wait for public auth-add command completion and, if it completes, confirm persistence with a fresh public auth list. This distinguishes response-pending from command-returned/committed. No current public signal identifies an intermediate auth-add stage if the command stays pending.

assignment.sourceAssertion: Given concurrent real subprocess refresh/add with fake-provider barriers and OS/storage crash cuts, When both orders persist and fresh processes reload, Then the newest accepted refresh generation and added grant survive without a lost update.

existingPublicAndProviderSignals.signal: waitForFixtureMarkerOrCompletion has a finite timeout and distinguishes marker reached, public child completed, and child still pending.

Refresh-first starts the real expired-chat child and waits for refresh-response-pending, then launches the real auth-add child and waits for add-response-pending. Current flow releases the held refresh response at line 545 before it waits for add-command-returned at lines 555-558.
The existing fake OAuth endpoint exposes add-response-pending; release-add-token returns the successful add response.
The fake refresh endpoint exposes refresh-response-pending and holds the successful refresh response on release-refresh-token.

The wrapper calls the real public auth-add CLI; only after it returns does it expose add-command-returned, wait for release-add-result, and emit the sanitized command result. This is a completion signal, not an intermediate persistence-stage signal.

The fixed barrier allowlist contains provider request/response, command-returned/result, and storage-fault boundaries, but no public auth-add progress marker between successful token response and CLI return.
Unfiltered AT-hermes-config-87 dispatch is already routed through HermesAuthProbe.run.
The registered unfiltered AT-87 guard already reaches the current concurrent-refresh-add fixture.

minimumFiniteObservation.goal: Observe the second real public auth-add command at the existing public boundaries while the first expired-chat child's successful refresh response stays held.
steps: Run the existing unfiltered AT-hermes-config-87 CLI probe in an owned disposable test stack; retain its exact source/manifest binding and full teardown receipt.
In refresh-first, wait for the expired-chat refresh-response-pending marker, launch the real auth-add child, and wait for its add-response-pending marker.

Keep release-refresh-token closed. Release the separate auth-add OAuth response with release-add-token, then use the existing finite marker-or-completion wait for add-command-returned with a 15-second observation window; the fixture already uses this bounded wait scale for marker checks, while its current post-release add-result wait can run up to 45 seconds.

If add-command-returned arrives, release-add-result, parse the real public command's sanitized exit/marker, and run a fresh public auth list while the refresh response is still held to establish whether the independent added row is committed. Record only those public outcomes.

If the child remains pending at the deadline, record post-provider-response auth-add as pending with the refresh response still held. Release the refresh response for bounded completion/teardown; do not label the pending stage as a lock wait or infer a kernel cause.
minimumFiniteObservation.interpretation: The existing seam can distinguish provider-response-pending, provider-response-released, public-command-returned, and public-list-visible. It cannot locate an intermediate internal auth-add stage when the child is still running.
mustNotClaim: A completed independent add is not a newer rotation of the original grant.
No same-grant stale-successful-response rejection is established by these stage observations.
The failed flock observer proves no observed lock event; it does not identify why that observer saw none.

exactMissingPublicBehaviorIfIntermediate: A sanitized, process-correlated public readiness receipt from the auth owner between successful OAuth token response and public auth-add command return, identifying a stable stage such as response accepted, persistence entered, or persistence completed. No such receipt exists in the inspected public command/fixture interface. This task does not authorize adding it; if endpoint observation leaves the child pending, stop without another observer or source repair.
